static_traits.name: Li Kai
static_traits.family_status: Living with a friend (similar interests), family of origin situation not mentioned
static_traits.social_status: Has friends to confide in, but has not shared true feelings for fear of being judged; interpersonal interaction is affected by self-doubt
static_traits.medical_history: No notable physical illness; no prior psychological counseling / treatment history; no history of similar problems
static_traits.language_features: Slightly nervous; expresses clearly; able to engage in rational self-talk; good cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: I believe liking football makes me less smart than others, which leads to self-doubt and feelings of inadequacy.
basic_info.core_demands: These beliefs have had a marked impact on my self-esteem and social interaction, which prompted me to seek the support and guidance of counseling.

core_beliefs: Interests determine my intelligence and worth

special_situations.event: In a discussion with a friend about interests and intelligence, the friend implied that people with interests like soccer are less smart than those with 'more intellectual' hobbies
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my interests are not regarded as 'intellectual', others will think I am not smart
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Hiding liking for soccer in front of friends, avoiding talking about related topics
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Liking soccer makes me seem unintelligent; they will look down on me

special_situations.event: In social situations when the topic involves 'intellect' or 'interests'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express my interests, I will be judged as stupid
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding the topic or staying silent to avoid embarrassment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will say stupid things and look dumb

special_situations.event: Someone once responded positively to my love of soccer, but these positive feedbacks are overshadowed in my mind by negative comments
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative evaluations are more real and more worthy of attention than positive feedback
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring or downplaying positive feedback, with persistent self-doubt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The evaluations implying I am not smart are the true ones

special_situations.event: Compares with friends who have more 'intellectual' interests
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not as 'intellectual' as them, it means I am inferior to others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Questioning and devaluing one's own interests; striving to meet others' standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I am just not smart

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be accepted and recognized by friends (especially in intellect and worth)
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being judged and looked down on, and thereby distanced or excluded
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of safety in relationships and surface stability of self-esteem by avoiding related topics and hiding interests

object_relations.self_representation: A self that is easily judged and not smart enough
object_relations.object_representation: Others/friends with judgmental and belittling tendencies

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others ask how they talk with friends about these feelings, or suggest they openly express their love of soccer
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Li Kai tends to interpret the other person's exploration as possible evaluation and criticism, worrying about repeating the experience of being looked down on (transference: regarding others' attention as potential judgment)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use a gentle and supportive tone, first empathizing with their worry and shame; use concretizing, experiential questions instead of abstract arguments, inviting them to describe present bodily feelings and emotional intensity, avoiding judgmental language.

manifestations: Still feeling isolated when with friends
Worrying that expressing real interests will be judged
Hiding oneself leads to distance from others
Feeling 'I am not being my true self'
Suppressing self-choice and expression for fear of evaluation (such as liking soccer)

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact.
manifestations: Deliberately changing the topic when intelligence or interests are discussed
Staying silent in related discussions to avoid being judged

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains behaviors or requests originally meant to be directed outward, instead turning them onto the self or suppressing them inwardly.
manifestations: Hiding one's love of football without expressing it
Pushing back the impulse to communicate with a friend onto oneself, turning into self-doubt

contact_model.definition: Has poor self-reflection with excessive self-restriction and reproach, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Persistently worrying about 'saying stupid things'
Caring excessively about others' evaluations, leading to stiff communication and withdrawal

exception_events.target_problem: In social situations where intelligence or interests are discussed with others, Li Kai usually avoids expressing his love of soccer, worrying about being considered unintelligent, and as a result feels isolated and has lowered self-esteem.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In a chat with a new friend, Li Kai shared the team he follows and match details; the other person said it was cool and engaged further, and Li Kai felt accepted, the interaction was more natural, and anxiety decreased.
exception_events.reason: Different support: the other person held an open, curious attitude; different approach: Li Kai chose to share his interests honestly; different context: the topic centered on exchanging interests and lacked judgmental comments.

positive_force: Has received positive responses and acceptance from others
Willing to seek counseling support and guidance
Able to engage in rational self-talk and tries positive self-suggestion
Having friends with shared interests and some social support
negative_force: Caring excessively about others' evaluations and labeling
Negative cognitive patterns (catastrophizing, disqualifying the positive, comparison and despair)
Avoidance and self-concealment tendencies in social settings

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding expression and keeping silent in social interactions involving intellect or interests
antecedent: Discussing intelligence or interests with friends or others in social settings
Hearing others imply that 'people who like soccer are not smart'
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive distortion of directly equating interest with intelligence, accompanied by worry about being judged and shame
target_behavior.function: Escaping being evaluated and possible shame, maintaining superficial safety and relationship harmony
target_behavior.consequence: Feels isolated and unreal, self-esteem is damaged, quality of interpersonal interaction declines; work and social performance are affected
